pairs.subject: native-shell-integration
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/model.ts:249 The unlock refusal maps UNSUPPORTED (the runtime's 'OS authentication is unsupported on this platform' / 'requires a supported Windows version', i.e. absent) to 'isn't set up', an action the user cannot take. It also maps UNAVAILABLE (which windows_native returns for 'Configure Windows Hello') to 'isn't ready right now… unlock again in a moment' (line 251). The presence and configuration classes come out swapped at the surface, so the refusal names the wrong cause.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/model.ts:249 Absent capability rendered as a not-configured one. Same wording at model.ts:171 for decisions and PairingConfirm.tsx:204 for the !native_reauth_available disclosure. On Windows supported() is always true, so that flag is false only on the non-Windows stub host, where 'set up' is impossible.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/gating.ts:3 The client only narrows. The selected deal and handoff values are never authority (selection.ts:41), and Rust re-derives label, token, lock and the selected deal.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/selection.ts:5 The view renders what Rust pushes and subscribes before it reads. It holds no connection of its own.

pairs.subject: native-shell-integration
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/forms.tsx:45 The lock indicator promises a Windows Hello unlock no matter what native_reauth_available says. The Tumbler receives that flag in settings:changed, and on the host where the runtime reports reauth absent the approval window disables unlock, so the two surfaces give contradictory disclosures of one capability's presence.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/forms.tsx:45 The disclosure ignores the presence predicate. Low severity (tooltip), but it is a surface inferring the class instead of reading it.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Tumbler.tsx:254 Rust owns the attention feed and pushes it. The page only re-reads on visibilitychange and on a 30s reconcile while a gate is open (WebView2 throttling is acknowledged at line 284).

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Tumbler.tsx:176 The omitted focus is written down. The page focuses its form only after a user-initiated open (lines 118-124). Natively, arrivals use set_focusable(false) and show_quietly (src-tauri events.rs:195).
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Tumbler.tsx:359 Acts send a single deal identity. Rust owns size, placement and the drag (Tumbler.tsx:1, tumbler_drag).
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/forms.tsx:359 An always-on-top annotator that never queries the application beneath it. Per the technique, an annotator does not need the third transparency.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Tumbler.tsx:496 Keys come straight from the desktop keyboard into the page. No host keeps keys and no wrapper forwards them.
